points.description: Names the time scale (the length of the process in time) as one of the two important scales in hydrology.
points.partial_credit: Half only if the scale is clearly about time (e.g. 'temporal') but the term 'time scale' or its meaning as length of the process is imprecise.

points.description: Names the spatial scale (the length scale of the process in space) as the other important scale in hydrology.
points.partial_credit: Half only if clearly about space/area (e.g. 'area scale') but the term 'spatial scale' is not used.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both scales named with the correct terms: time (temporal) scale and spatial (length) scale. Each is worth 1 mark; a vague or generic answer (e.g. 'large and small scale') earns nothing. A wrong extra scale, such as 'availability of drinking water' given as a scale, costs the point it accompanies; ignore it only if clearly just a descriptor.
